conceptZh: 「羊」變成毛線圍巾架，小玩具羊拉下短短的圍巾，竟捲出比自己大好幾倍的毛線球。
object: A solid teal 羊 sculpture, a wool scarf, and a tiny wind-up toy sheep
morph: The glyph remains structurally unchanged while a scarf unwinds from its lowest horizontal stroke into an absurdly oversized yarn ball.
creativeAngle: 把完整字形當成圍巾架，利用短圍巾竟拉出巨大毛線球的尺寸反差製造笑點；不靠羊角或臉部變形，確保六筆清楚。
promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second animated toy comedy in a softly lit peach studio, with a locked frontal camera. Center one correctly formed Traditional Chinese glyph 羊, built as a flat-faced, saturated teal toy sculpture occupying approximately 70% of frame height with generous margins. Use standard textbook glyph proportions: two distinct upper marks, three separate horizontal strokes, and one central vertical stroke. Keep its silhouette rigid and its strokes clearly distinguishable throughout. A cream wool scarf hangs over the lowest horizontal stroke without concealing its outline; its folded length is tucked behind that bar. A tiny wind-up toy sheep stands beside the scarf's dangling end. From 0.0–1.4 seconds, the sheep takes the end in its mouth and gives a small tug, then pauses expectantly. From 1.4–3.5 seconds, the surprisingly long scarf unravels into yarn that the sheep enthusiastically winds with a little mechanical tail spindle. The ball grows to three times the sheep's height; the sheep stops winding and slowly looks up at its ridiculous achievement. From 3.5–4.6 seconds, one gentle nudge sends the lightweight ball rolling out to the right, with the sheep trotting after it. Keep this action beside the centered glyph and fully within the frame until the deliberate exit. From 4.6–8.0 seconds, hold the completely bare 羊 motionless and unobstructed, preserving its full height and margins. Use tactile felt and painted wood textures, bright restrained colors, soft shadows, and gentle comic movement. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin, saying exactly 「羊、羊、綿羊」: the first 羊 around 0.5 seconds, the second around 2.0 seconds, and 綿羊 around 5.3 seconds during the clear final hold. Leave natural pauses and stop after the word. Add only quiet wool-rustling and toy-winding sounds beneath the voice. The single 羊 is the only on-screen text; keep the vocabulary audio-only, with no subtitles, other lettering, watermark, clutter, or flashing effects.

conceptZh: 兔子魔術師輕敲「羊」的三條橫畫施法，帽子卻冒出一隻蓬鬆綿羊，把正在偷看的兔子頂成仰躺姿勢。
object: A rigid teal 羊 sculpture, an original cartoon magician rabbit with a top hat, and one round cartoon sheep.
morph: The glyph remains correctly formed and stationary; tapping its three horizontal strokes summons a sheep whose expanding fleece gently tips the rabbit backward.
creativeAngle: 把三條橫畫當成施法的觸點，改用魔術帽冒出過度蓬鬆綿羊的失誤笑點；字形全程固定，不再使用圍巾或毛線球，也不讓羊毛遮住筆畫。
promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second animated comedy with tactile felt characters and a locked frontal camera in a bright, softly lit pale-apricot studio. Center one solid saturated-teal Traditional Chinese glyph 羊, occupying about 70% of frame height with comfortable margins. Use a standard textbook form: two separate inward-slanting upper marks, three distinct horizontal strokes, and a central vertical stroke crossing all three horizontals and extending below the lowest. Preserve this rigid, readable silhouette throughout.

The lead is an original, theatrically confident cartoon magician rabbit with floppy ears and a plum top hat. Its only supporting character is one round cream-colored cartoon sheep. Stage their action beside the glyph in the generous right-hand space of a wide composition, with every character fully framed.

At 0.0–1.3 seconds, the rabbit removes its hat, sets it opening-up beside the glyph, and confidently taps the right endpoint of each of the three horizontal strokes in descending order. Its small paw briefly touches only the endpoints. At 1.3–2.4 seconds, nothing happens. The rabbit straightens proudly, notices the empty hat, then bends close to inspect it. At 2.4–3.6 seconds, a tiny sheep head peeks out; its unexpectedly enormous, soft spherical fleece rises underneath the rabbit's chin and gently rolls the rabbit backward onto the wool, paws pointing upward. The sheep gives one quiet bleat while the rabbit blinks in baffled surprise. Keep the entire fleece to the right of the glyph. At 3.6–4.7 seconds, the sheep steps free of the hat and its fleece settles to a compact round shape, lowering the rabbit gently onto its feet. The rabbit retrieves its hat and gives a sheepish little bow beside its successful creation.

From 4.7–8.0 seconds, hold the centered, fully unobstructed 羊 completely still; the rabbit and sheep remain quietly posed beside it. No camera movement or new action during this final hold.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin, saying exactly 「羊、羊、綿羊」. Place the first 羊 around 0.4 seconds, the second around 1.7 seconds, and 綿羊 around 5.4 seconds while the finished glyph remains clearly visible. Stop after the word. Use only soft tapping, felt rustling, and the quiet bleat beneath the voice, without music. The single 羊 is the only visible text; the vocabulary is audio only. No subtitles, logos, watermark, clutter, or flashing effects.

conceptZh: 消防小隊的水管亂噴，輕輕碰倒第一根積木，連鎖骨牌倒下，兩個彎角、三條橫線和一條直線剛好落成「羊」，毛茸茸的小綿羊蹦出來。
object: a chunky toy fire engine, a floppy fire hose with a mind of its own, a row of wooden domino blocks and a fluffy toy lamb
morph: a line of dominoes topples and lands as the two horns, three bars and the upright of 羊
creativeAngle: 骨牌連鎖：水管一抖碰倒第一塊骨牌，骨牌依序倒成羊角、三條橫線與中間一豎，最後小綿羊從消防車後面探出頭。
promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second animated comedy with a locked frontal camera, bright and energetic, no flashing. Setting: a clean solid pale-yellow backdrop with a pale mint floor line. The only on-screen text is one bold, saturated tangerine-orange Traditional Chinese glyph 羊, with two short horn strokes at the top, three horizontal bars below them and a long vertical down the middle, centered, uncropped, filling about 70% of frame height with margins. The lead is an original chunky red toy fire engine with a round smiling face on its grille and a floppy yellow hose that has a mind of its own, plus a small toy crew dog in a helmet standing by; no real people. Moment one (0.0-1.8s): the fire engine rolls in with a bright toot, the hose uncoils and flops about like a noodle, and the first spoken 羊 lands as the nozzle tips the very first orange domino standing at the left; the crew dog jumps in alarm. Moment two (1.8-3.4s): a chain of orange dominoes topples across the floor in a wave, the first two curving up into the horns, with a splash of water droplets from the hose arcing over them for a rainbow; the second spoken 羊 lands as a domino spins in the air and drops into place as the first bar. Moment three (3.4-5.0s): the remaining dominoes clack down in sequence, laying down the second and third bars and the long upright stripe, the hose whipping one last time and tangling around the engine's bumper; the word 綿羊 is spoken as the last domino plops down, and from behind the engine a fluffy white toy lamb pops its head up, surprised. From 5.0-8.0s the glyph 羊 is completely still, unobstructed and crisp in orange; the lamb hops up and down at the side with a little bleating wiggle, the crew dog salutes and the engine's lights spin slowly, never touching the strokes. Narration (off-screen only, warm Taiwanese Mandarin, slow, distinct, clear tones, no erhua): the voice says exactly 「羊、羊、綿羊」, read as ㄧㄤˊ、ㄧㄤˊ、ㄇㄧㄢˊ ㄧㄤˊ, first utterance at about 0.6s, second at about 2.8s, the word at about 4.5s, then stop with no repeats and no extra speech. No background music. No subtitles, no vocabulary text, no watermark, no clutter.

conceptZh: 積木小隊疊成撞門槌，想撞開布忍者躲的小紙牆，第一次半路自己倒掉，第二次全速撞上牆「砰」地散開，六塊積木剛好落成「羊」，牆後蹦出一隻玩具山羊。
object: a squad of six chunky orange interlocking building bricks (two short, three long flat bars, one tall column) plus a tiny captain brick, stacked into a battering-ram tower
morph: the crash scatters the bricks upward; the two short bricks land tilted as the top marks, the three bars drop in as the three horizontals, the tall column slots down through the middle as the vertical stroke
creativeAngle: 前三版都是圍巾、魔術帽、骨牌等慢慢變化，這版改成六歲孩子一眼看懂的「衝撞」：積木小隊先疊高、往後拉弓，第一次半路自己垮掉（符合「最糟時刻倒下」的個性），第二次真的撞上牆，撞散的積木直接落成羊字。詞改用「山羊」，撞牆後牆後面蹦出玩具山羊，聲音和畫面同一個故事，也呼應羊字頂上像角的兩點。
promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second animated slapstick short, locked frontal camera, bright and clean, no flashing. Setting: a solid pale-cream backdrop with a soft mint floor line, nothing else behind. The only on-screen text will be one bold, saturated orange Traditional Chinese glyph 羊, built from toy bricks, finishing centered and uncropped at about 70% of frame height with clear margins.

The lead is an original squad of six chunky, glossy orange interlocking building bricks with tiny dot eyes: two short stubby bricks, three long flat bars and one tall column, led by a pint-sized captain brick wearing a paper helmet. They march in a proud line, stack themselves eagerly and topple at the worst possible moment. The single supporting character is an original tiny grey felt ninja standing at the far right behind a cardboard wall that is far too short; his feet, elbows and mask tip stick out everywhere, yet he holds perfectly still, certain he is invisible.

Moment one, 0.0 to 1.5 seconds: the squad marches in from the left, the captain brick spots the ninja's exposed feet and points dramatically. The bricks clack together into a tall battering-ram tower, dig in at the base and lean way back in a long cartoon wind-up while the captain waves them on.

Moment two, 1.5 to 3.0 seconds: the tower charges, but halfway across the floor it wobbles, buckles and flops over in a clattering heap short of the wall. The jolt makes the ninja's smoke bomb pop by accident in a small harmless grey puff above his head; the ninja freezes even harder, still sure nobody can see him.

Moment three, 3.0 to 4.8 seconds: the bricks spring up, restack faster into an even taller tower, lean back twice as far, then rocket right and hit the cardboard wall with a big squashy BONK. The wall folds flat, the tower squashes like an accordion and six bricks fly up in a clean arc and drop into the center of the frame as the glyph 羊: the two short bricks land tilted inward as the two top marks, the three bars stack in as three evenly spaced horizontal strokes, and the tall column slots straight down through all three, poking out below the lowest bar. Use standard textbook proportions for 羊, every stroke distinct and separated. The captain brick ricochets off the wall and tumbles out to the lower right, squashed slightly flat, with a dizzy grin.

Moment four, 4.8 to 8.0 seconds: the orange 羊 stands completely still, crisp and unobstructed for the whole final hold. From behind the flattened wall a small white-and-tan toy goat with curly horns pops up, blinks, and gently nudges the flattened ninja, who finally stands and strikes a sheepish ninja pose. The dizzy captain brick wobbles in a little circle and ends in a proud salute. None of them touch or cover the strokes.

Narration, off-screen only, a warm friendly voice in slow, distinct Taiwanese Mandarin with clear tones and no erhua: the voice says exactly 「羊、羊、山羊」, read exactly as ㄧㄤˊ、ㄧㄤˊ、ㄕㄢ ㄧㄤˊ. The first 羊 lands at about 0.7 seconds as the bricks begin stacking into the tower; the second 羊 lands at about 4.3 seconds as the final column slots into place and the glyph snaps complete; 山羊 is spoken at about 5.6 seconds exactly as the toy goat pops up behind the fallen wall, with the finished 羊 clearly visible. Stop after the word, with no repeats and no extra speech. Only soft brick clacks, one cushioned cartoon bonk and a tiny puff sound beneath the voice; no music. Tactile glossy plastic, felt and cardboard textures, bright but not neon, soft shadows, no white blowouts. No subtitles, no vocabulary text, no other lettering, no watermark, no clutter.
